paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God cares about the details when He builds a place to live among His people. Every curtain, every clasp, every post had its spot, and none of it was left to guess. God told Moses to set it up "according to the pattern shown you on the mountain" (Exodus 26:30). So the plan wasn't Moses' idea or Israel's idea, it was God's, and that's a big relief for anybody who has ever tried to wing it.

Now look at how the whole thing is laid out. A curtain of blue, purple and scarlet hangs at the entrance, a veil separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, and the ark sits behind it (Exodus 26:33, 36). There's an altar out in the courtyard, with a gate that lets people in (Exodus 27:1, 16). I think the lesson is that you don't just wander up to God however you please, you come the way He says. And friend, He is the one who made the way, so the instructions are a gift and not a lecture.

Then the passage ends with lamps that keep burning, tended by Aaron and his sons "from evening until morning," as "a permanent statute for the Israelites for the generations to come" (Exodus 27:21). That tells me God's plan for living among His people wasn't a quick weekend project. He's patient, He's steady, and He keeps the light on. So bring that to your day, baker: the God who planned every clasp and every lamp has a plan for you, and He is never rushed. And this story isn't over, because God still has more to tell Moses on that mountain.
